The Masquerade Auction: Last Bid
The last lot is the right to keep his secret. He bids one dollar.
At a masked auction where silence is sold sealed in wax, Adrian bids a dollar on his own secret — and five dangerous people must decide who gets to own it.

Every year the House of Vellum auctions the right to keep a secret sealed; whatever goes unsold is read aloud at dawn. Adrian walks in with one dollar and one rule: nobody buys him. Lucien holds a council seat and could end it all in one bid; Dante has already bought Cass's secret without asking; Nikolai keeps the House rules and wants to know exactly what breaking them costs. You decide what Adrian lets anyone pay for — and what he says in his own voice.
The adult auction coordinator who hands out the paddles — and knows which envelopes are still unsold.
If nobody changes the rules, every unsold secret is read aloud at dawn — and every bought one belongs to someone else forever.

One Dollar
Find out whether any proxy is actually authorized
The auction floor
Saturday, 11:40 PM
Masks, candles, a hundred quiet paddles. On the dais, Nikolai lifts a black envelope sealed in red wax. Lot forty-nine: the sealing of A. Vale.
Opening at ten thousand.
I raise paddle forty-nine. My paddle. My lot. On the back, in marker, I've written one dollar.
That's not a bid.
It's what your right to my silence is worth.
Laughter ripples, then stops. Across the room, Lucien Marchetti keeps his paddle in his lap and does not lift it.
I send a card by steward, in my own hand: May I bid on your behalf? Yes or no. Either answer stands.
He could end this with one number. That's exactly the problem.
What does Adrian do with Lucien's card?
Authorize him: repeat my bid, nothing more.
I write on the back: Proxy granted. One sentence only — the bidder stands at one dollar. Revocable at any time.
I stand and say exactly that, in exactly those words, and sit back down. It costs me nothing but the room's opinion.
Unusual. Noted. Lot forty-nine is held until I verify the terms.
Adrian granted Lucien a narrow, revocable proxy to repeat his one-dollar bid; Lucien said only that, and Nikolai held the lot.
Not yet. Ask Nikolai for a recess.
Steward. I request a recess on my own lot. House rule twelve.
You've read the rules. Rare. Fifteen minutes.
I put Lucien's card in my pocket, unanswered. Across the room he nods, like that's an answer too.
Adrian left Lucien's card unanswered and invoked a fifteen-minute recess on his own lot.
Tear up the card. Handle this yourself.
I tear the card in half, slowly, so he can see. Nobody speaks for me tonight. Not even politely.
A masked stranger bids twelve thousand on Adrian's secret. Lucien sets his paddle face down on the floor and leaves it there.
Bidding resumes at midnight. Mr. Vale, your dollar stands. It is not winning.
Adrian tore up Lucien's proxy card; a stranger bid on his lot, Lucien set his paddle down, and bidding paused until midnight.
Still Owned by You
Stop anyone buying a secret without asking
Backstage corridor
Saturday, 11:58 PM
Behind the velvet, the House is all stone and cold air. Adrian goes looking for water and finds Cass instead, holding a paid receipt.
Lot thirty-one. C. Reyes, sealed. Purchased by D. Moretti at eleven fifty-two. I never raised a paddle.
You paid before you asked.
I wanted it gone.
Gone from them. Still owned by you.
I look past him at the one with the dollar paddle. He seems to know the House rules better than the House does.
Tell him it's protection.
It is protection. It's also a leash with a nicer price tag.
Dante wants Adrian on his side. What does Adrian say?
Tell Dante: hand Cass the envelope.
Protection is when he asks for it. Give him the envelope. Unopened.
I take it from my jacket. Red wax, unbroken. I hold it out and keep my hand steady. That's the hard part.
I take it. I don't open it. Not here, not for him, not for anyone.
Down the corridor, Lucien waits by a door marked COUNCIL. 'Once a century, a guest may propose a rule,' he says. 'Tonight's the night. Interested?'
Adrian told Dante to return Cass's sealed envelope; Dante handed it over unopened, and Lucien revealed a guest could propose a rule to the council tonight.
Say nothing. Hold the door for them.
Not my secret, not my call. I step back and hold the stage door so they have somewhere quiet to finish this.
We'll talk. Not tonight. And you don't open it.
I won't.
Down the corridor, Lucien waits by a door marked COUNCIL. 'Once a century, a guest may propose a rule,' he says. 'Tonight's the night. Interested?'
Adrian stayed out of it and held the door; Cass told Dante they'd talk later and not to open the envelope, and Lucien told Adrian a guest could propose a rule tonight.
Walk away. This isn't your fight.
I go back the way I came. I have my own envelope to worry about.
Behind him, the argument drops to a register no one else can hear. The receipt stays crushed in Cass's fist.
At the stairs, Lucien blocks nothing. He just waits. 'Once a century, a guest may propose a rule. Tonight's the night. Interested?'
Adrian walked away from Cass and Dante's argument; at the stairs Lucien told him a guest could propose a rule to the council tonight.
Only Your Own
Propose that each person may bid only on their own seal
The council room, upstairs
Sunday, 12:20 AM
Twelve chairs, eleven masks, one ledger the size of a tombstone. Nikolai presides. Dante and Cass stand at the back, not touching.
One rule. Every person may bid only on the sealing of their own secret. Nobody buys anyone else's.
Then the room loses its entertainment.
It can survive being bored.
A rule change needs a seconder with a seat. And the House will want to know who pays for its lost night.
Every mask turns to me. I could second him. I could also just buy the night and spare everyone the vote.
Money would end it faster. Money would also mean it's still for sale.
What does Adrian ask of Lucien?
Ask Lucien to second the rule. Not buy it.
Second it. In your own name. Don't pay for it.
Seconded. My name, my seat. Not my wallet.
Nikolai calls the vote. Seven to four. The ledger takes a new line in red ink: One may only buy one's own silence.
Lucien seconded Adrian's rule in his own name without paying; the council passed 'one may only buy one's own silence' seven to four.
Just cancel it. Keep everyone at a distance.
I don't need a seconder who'll want to be thanked. Cancel the auction. That's all I'm asking.
Cancellation without a rule. Then it happens again next year.
I vote for the cancellation and nothing more. I don't look at him while I do it. He asked for distance. He gets it.
Adrian asked only for a cancellation and kept his distance; Lucien voted for it without seconding any new rule.
Let Lucien's money end it.
Fine. You have the money. End it.
If you ask, I will. Understand what it makes me: every sealed envelope in this House, with my name on each one.
He buys every remaining lot in one bid. Nikolai stamps the ledger. The room exhales. Nothing has changed except who owns it all.
Adrian asked Lucien to buy out the auction; Lucien bought every remaining lot and became the owner of every sealed secret.
Withdrawn
Proxies can be withdrawn — no secret read to justify it
The council room
Sunday, 1:05 AM
Cass crosses the council room and sets a proxy card on the table in front of Dante. Across from them, Lucien slides his paddle into his coat.
I can withdraw this.
Yes.
Say that before the bid.
Then there is no bid yet.
The room will object. Objections require justification. Mr. Vale, read your lot into the record.
It can object without owning an answer.
Eleven masks wait for wax to break. Adrian's envelope sits in front of him, unopened.
Nikolai wants the secret read. What does Adrian do?
Refuse to read it. Withdraw anyway.
I put my hand flat on the envelope. Not opening it. Holding it closed.
Withdrawal doesn't need a reason. That's the whole point of it.
I check the old charter. He's right, and it irritates me. I write it in: a proxy may be withdrawn, unread.
Adrian refused to read his secret, and Nikolai entered into the charter that a proxy may be withdrawn without justification.
Name the category. Keep the secret.
It's about my family. That's all the record gets.
Category noted. Content sealed. Acceptable. Barely.
I write one word on my own card: Personal. It's enough. It always should have been.
Adrian named only the category of his secret, family, and Cass did the same; the council accepted both withdrawals without content.
Walk out of the vote.
I stand, push my chair in, and leave the council room. My envelope stays on the table. Closed.
The objection stands without him. We vote without him.
I don't follow him. I stay and vote the way he told me he would. That's all I'm allowed to do.
Adrian walked out rather than justify himself; Lucien stayed and voted as Adrian had said he would, without following him.
The Cost of Cancelling
Everyone pays their own share of cancelling
The auction floor, emptied
Sunday, 2:10 AM
The House loses one night's revenue. Someone covers it. Each of you names what you'll give up. No one pledges another person's secret.
My buyout of lot thirty-one. Refunded to the House. I keep nothing.
My mask. I'll stand here without it until dawn.
My gavel. One year. Someone else can keep these rules.
My seat on the council.
That buys the cancellation. It doesn't buy me.
I know.
Everyone else paid with something they had. I've got a dollar and a name.
What does Adrian put on the table?
Your dollar and your name, unmasked.
I take off my mask and set my dollar on the ledger. Adrian Vale. No secret attached. Just the face.
I record it at full value. It is worth exactly what he says. That has never once happened in this House.
I don't look at his face too long. He didn't take the mask off for me.
Adrian unmasked and paid his one dollar under his own name; Nikolai recorded it at full value toward the cancellation.
Accept the split. Put Lucien's terms in writing.
Write it down. His seat pays the House. It doesn't pay me, doesn't buy a drink, doesn't buy a door.
I write every word. Lucien initials it without being asked.
Good. Now it's true on paper, too.
Adrian had Nikolai record that Lucien's seat paid only the House and bought nothing from Adrian; Lucien initialed it.
Refuse Lucien's seat. Keep your lot in play.
Keep your seat. I'll take my chances at dawn.
I take my seat back. It's the hardest thing I've done all year, and I do it in silence.
The other lots are cancelled. Lot forty-nine is not. The House clock reads 2:14. Dawn is at 6:31.
Adrian refused Lucien's sacrifice; the other lots were cancelled, but Adrian's own lot stayed in play until dawn.
One Question
An invitation for one drink, no negotiation
The House bar, behind the floor
Sunday, 3:30 AM
The candles are mostly stubs. Adrian sits at the House bar with his mask beside him. Lucien stops a polite distance away.
One question. You can ask it. I don't have to answer.
I have a hundred questions. I pick the smallest one, because it's the one I mean.
Will you stay for one drink?
One. No negotiations.
None. I'll pour. You'll pay. A dollar, if you like.
He remembered. Of course he remembered. That's the dangerous part.
How does Adrian take the drink?
Stay for one drink. No terms.
I slide my dollar across the bar. He pours. We drink like two people who've agreed on something.
This is the first thing tonight nobody bid on.
Keep it that way.
Adrian stayed for one drink with Lucien, paid his own dollar, and asked that it stay unbought.
Stay — at the long table, with everyone.
One drink. Out there. With everyone.
At the long table, Cass sits unmasked, Dante one chair away, Nikolai doing sums on a napkin. Lucien takes the seat across, not beside.
Nobody buys a round. Everyone pays for their own.
Adrian accepted the drink but moved it to the long table with everyone; Lucien sat across from him, not beside him.
Decline. Leave the mask. Take the door.
Not tonight. Thanks for asking instead of buying.
I leave my mask on the bar and walk out under the stone arch. Nobody stops me. The door was never locked.
I set his mask on the shelf behind the bar, where it'll be if he wants it. Not where I can keep it.
Adrian declined the drink and left; Lucien set the mask where Adrian could reclaim it, not where he could keep it.
Masks Stop Working
Each pair answers for itself — cancelling isn't romance
The long table
Sunday, 5:40 AM
Dawn is fifty minutes out. Adrian takes off his mask for good and sets a glass on the table across from Lucien.
One question?
One. I may not answer.
Will you stay until the glass is empty?
I can do that.
At the far end, Cass stands, the envelope in his breast pocket. Dante half-rises with him.
Dante, not tonight.
Then I will not follow you out.
The glass is half full. When it's empty, I'm the one who decides what that means.
When the glass is empty, what does Adrian say?
Stay past the glass. Say you want to.
Glass is empty. I'm staying anyway. That's not a negotiation. It's what I want.
Then I'll want it out loud too. I'd like to see you tomorrow. Unmasked. Unbought.
Yes.
Adrian chose to stay past the empty glass and said so; Lucien asked to see him tomorrow, and Adrian said yes.
Finish the glass. Ask for slow.
Glass is empty. I like this. I want it slower than tonight was.
Slow is a speed I'm good at.
Cass leaves alone. Dante doesn't follow. Two pairs of people, separately, choose not to rush.
Adrian finished the drink and asked to go slowly; Lucien agreed without pushing, and Cass left without Dante following.
Finish the glass. Say a real goodbye.
That's the glass. Thank you for asking every time. This is where I get off.
I stand when he does. I don't offer my hand unless he offers his. He does. Once.
Then goodbye, Adrian. Properly.
Adrian finished the drink and said goodbye; Lucien shook his hand once, only after Adrian offered it, and let him go.
Last Bid
Choose disclosure, sealing — and each other, or not
The auction floor at dawn
Sunday, 6:31 AM
Dawn through the high windows. By House law, unsold lots are read now. Nikolai stands at the dais without his gavel, holding Adrian's envelope.
Mr. Vale. By whatever rule tonight left standing, this one is yours to decide.
I break my own wax in the corridor, alone, and read my secret to nobody. Then I burn it. Mine.
I watch the smoke from a respectful distance. I don't ask what it said. I'm learning.
I stay in my seat. I could stand beside him. I wait to be asked.
Seal it, say it, or walk out with it. For the first time tonight, nobody else gets a vote.
What does Adrian do with lot forty-nine?
Seal it yourself. Sit with Lucien as equals.
I put the envelope in my own pocket — sealed by me, owned by me — and sit down next to Lucien. Beside, not across.
Dante. Ask me tomorrow. Properly.
Tomorrow. I'll ask first.
Same table tomorrow. Nobody bids.
Adrian sealed his own secret and sat beside Lucien as an equal; Cass invited Dante to ask him properly tomorrow.
Seal it. Walk out alone. Leave the door open.
I pocket the envelope and walk out alone into a grey Sunday.
I let the door close behind him. I don't follow. If he wants a second drink, he knows where the bar is.
I leave by the side door. Dante leaves by the front. Nobody follows anyone.
The auction's over. That's all tonight was.
Adrian sealed his own secret and left alone; the auction was cancelled, and everyone went their separate ways without romance.
Read aloud only what you choose. Then leave.
I break the wax and read the first line aloud — the part I'm willing to say — and fold the rest back into my pocket.
That's my secret. I said it. Nobody owns it now.
Dante's proxy card is still in my hand. I tear it in half, gently, and set both pieces in front of him.
The bids made for others still sit in the ledger. Adrian walks past them, out the unlocked door, and nobody tries to buy what he said.
Adrian read aloud only the part he chose and left; Cass refused Dante's proxy by tearing it, and the bids made for others stayed in the ledger.
Nobody Bids
The own-secret rule holds, and both pairs get to talk as equals. Adrian keeps his envelope sealed in his own pocket and his seat beside Lucien, and Cass tells Dante to ask him properly tomorrow.
Same table tomorrow. Nobody bids.
Cancelled
The auction is cancelled and no secret is read, but nobody pretends it was romance. Everyone leaves by a different door, free to come back — or not.
The auction's over. That's all tonight was.
Said Out Loud
The bidding for others never fully stops, so Adrian takes the one exit nobody can buy: he says what he chooses, in his own voice, and walks out. Cass hands Dante his proxy back, torn in two.
That's my secret. I said it. Nobody owns it now.
